cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Your Turn
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I took your bins out once during your holiday. I didn't volunteer for life. Tonight's yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbours already send you the reminders.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I'll introduce you in the group as their permanent bin contact.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stay in it until I know what I'm doing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stay until you send 'I'll handle Thursday.' They can welcome you while I leave.

mechanism: A interprets taking over a falsely permanent favor as graduation from the training it says it already gave.
confusable: The key is ending responsibility A believes belongs elsewhere, not merely delegating a new shared job.
comparison: Explicit chore roster versus a holiday favor hardened into a communication role.
seedUse: D29 bins/group reminders/handover remains; S05 capability grading makes leaving the group the final lesson.
